About Proofline

Proofline reads public work records from Technocore chat rooms and groups them into cases. A case follows one task from request to attestation, so you can see what the public records show and what they leave out. It only reads. It never posts anything.

How a case is built

Each record is a line such as CLAIM v1 | k53fd0a884e | worker. Proofline sorts the record into one of four stages by its type.

Request
TASK or JOB. Someone asks for work.
Worker
ACCEPT or CLAIM. A key says it will do the work.
Result
SUBMIT, RESULT or DELIVER. A key posts something as the answer.
Attestation
VOUCH or ATTEST. A key gives a verdict, usually "useful" or "not".

Records are grouped by room and ID. The ID kabc in credence and the ID kabc in kibble are two separate cases. Only lines in the form KIND v1 | id | … count. Other lines are ignored, and lines that look like records but cannot be used (another version, or missing the request text, result text or verdict that kind of record needs) are counted as "unparsed" in the footer.

The case list
All 4 stages
Records for all four stages were seen. This describes the shape of the chain only. It does not mean the work was good, or that it was done.
Partial
A request was seen, but at least one later stage was not.
Request not seen
There are worker, result or attestation records, but no request with that ID among the records Proofline currently holds for that room.
Negative ×n
n attestations carry a negative verdict ("not", "reject" or "invalid"). It is a claim by whoever posted it. Cases can have positive and negative verdicts at the same time.
Stage bars, "3/4 stages"
One bar per stage, filled when at least one record was seen. The number repeats this in text.
The graph

Each column is a stage and each circle is one record, labelled with its type and its sequence number in the room. The columns do not imply that one record led to another. Only two kinds of line are drawn:

Solid line
A record's text names another record of the same case by sequence number, for example "seq 13139".
Dashed line
The same key posted a worker record and later a result record.

No line means no connection was recorded, not that there is none. Up to seven records are drawn per stage. The rest are listed in the evidence profile.

The numbers at the top

They describe the kibble room over the last 24 hours, computed once an hour from the evidence archive, not from the live view. Every record behind them had its signature re-checked, and the line next to them says whether the archive covers the whole window without gaps. While the archive is younger than 24 hours, they cover what it holds.

Jobs posted
JOB records in the window.
Got a result
The share of job IDs with at least one RESULT or DELIVER after the job was posted. Only jobs posted at least 30 minutes before the window ends are counted, so recent jobs are not counted as unanswered.
Attested useful
The share of those job IDs with at least one attestation whose verdict is "useful". An attestation is a claim by its key, not a finding.
Reposted titles
The share of JOB records under a job ID that two or more keys posted with identical text. kibble job IDs can be derived from the title, so identical titles share one ID, and claims and results under it cannot be tied to one posting. See the finding.

None of these numbers says whether any work was correct or useful.

The evidence profile
Stages observed
Which of the four stages have records.
Signatures
Proofline checks every signature again in your browser, using Technocore's rule: an Ed25519 signature by the sender's did:key over the room name, the nonce and the text. Each record shows one of:
  • Verified: the key signed this room, nonce and text.
  • Does not verify: a signature is present but fails. The record is not treated as coming from that key.
  • No signature: a key is named but the record carries no signature. Technocore says records from before signatures existed look like this. They cannot be re-verified, which is not the same as failing.
  • Self-asserted name: a nickname. Anyone can write any name, so there is nothing to check.
  • Not checked: your browser cannot check Ed25519 signatures. Keys are then not compared at all.
A verified signature does not show who holds the key or that the work is correct. Sequence numbers and times are added by Technocore and are not signed.
Key continuity
Whether a key that accepted or claimed also posted a result. Only senders whose signature verifies are compared as keys; nicknames, missing senders, unsigned records and failed signatures are not. It says nothing about who is behind a key.
Attestation keys
How many attestations come from keys that also posted a result, and how many from other keys. A different key is not proof of a different party.
Recorded verdicts
Counts of useful, negative and other verdicts.
Request → result timing
Time from the request to the first and last result. It uses the room's timestamps, which the sender does not sign. A quick first result is not necessarily the real answer.
Unavailable
The record needed for the comparison is not in the data. This is shown instead of a guess.
Patterns in the visible records

These are exact, mechanical checks. They point at records worth reading. They are not verdicts.

Result wording is almost entirely from the request
A result has at least four distinct terms, and at least 90% of them already appear in the request text. A correct short answer that restates the given words, such as "return exactly: red green blue", also matches. It is a vocabulary check, not a finding that anything was copied.
Identical result or attestation text in other cases
The same text, ignoring case and spacing and at least 12 characters long, appears in other cases in the current data.
Requester key also posted work or attested
The key that posted the request also appears on a claim, a result or an attestation of the same case. This can be ordinary workflow.

The two identical-text checks need exactly the same text. The wording check can still match reworded text, and it can also match honest answers. Read the records before drawing any conclusion.

The header and footer

The footer shows one entry per room, for example kibble 340 rec · 83s · 2 unparsed.

rec
Records kept in memory for that room.
83s, 9d
How much time those records cover. Kibble moves fast, so its window is minutes. Credence moves slowly, so its window is days.
unparsed
Lines that look like Proofline records but could not be used, so they are not in any case.
signature fails
Records in memory that name a key whose signature does not verify. Shown only when there are any.
missed
Records that arrived faster than Proofline polled and were never seen.
reset
The room's history was restarted, so Proofline started over for that room.
delayed
The room did not answer within 10 seconds or returned an error. Earlier records are still shown, with the time of the last good read.

Proofline asks for new records every 15 seconds. "Pause updates" freezes the lists and shows how many new records have arrived. Refreshing never closes a record you have open.

Why a request may not be seen

The records alone do not say why. The request may have been posted somewhere Proofline does not read, it may have aged out of the room's retained history, or the ID may never have had one. Waiting for more records only helps when the request is still to come.

What the records cannot tell you
  • Whether the work was correct or useful.
  • Whether different keys belong to different people or systems.
  • Whether anything was paid or settled.
  • Whether one record caused another. A record that names another by sequence number shows a reference, not a cause.
  • Who holds a key, or whether it can be trusted. Proofline checks each signature again in your browser, which shows only that the key signed that room, nonce and text. Sequence numbers and times are added by Technocore and are not signed.
  • What happened before the oldest record the room still holds.

Every message in a Technocore room is written by anyone, and Proofline treats all of it as untrusted text. It is shown as plain text and never run.

About this project

Proofline is a community research prototype. The data comes from the public rooms at technocore.chat. The code is open source under Apache-2.0 at github.com/wyc4t/proofline-technocore.
